meta.title: Power under pressure
meta.subtitle: Climate risk to the power sector
meta.source: IRENA assessment, Annex 4 and Annex 5, annual aggregation

heat.name: Heatwaves
heat.ind: TX95 – number of very hot days

MEAS.imp: Damage to dam walls and turbines, directly or from debris carried from flooded areas upstream. Water released through bypass channels reduces output.
m: Build or reinforce defence structures for dams and turbines, such as check dams and dykes
Adjust water management, for example retention ponds that store excess water and release it gradually
Restore reservoir storage capacity by dredging
Assess options to increase storage, such as raising dams or building water transfer works
Carry out bathymetric surveys more often to track loss of volume to sediment
Consider vortex, hydrokinetic or hydro-screw turbines at plant outlets and along rivers
Install floating solar PV on reservoirs and on the land around them

MEAS.imp: Damage to infrastructure, lower output from debris, electrical hazards.
m: Raise inverters and electrical equipment above flood levels
Use robust foundations, sealed wiring and corrosion-resistant structures
Design site drainage and retention areas, and keep water out of electrical conduits
Plant native pollinator vegetation to absorb stormwater and limit erosion

MEAS.imp: Dust and debris on panels lower efficiency and can damage modules.
m: Schedule cleaning, including automated cleaning controlled by sensors
Use anti-soiling coatings and measure soiling rates regularly
Set panel tilt to help dust slide off
Add storage to cover periods of low hydropower output
Study cloud cover and solar resource where more dry days are projected, to find room for more solar

MEAS.imp: Lower panel efficiency, thermal degradation, hot spots and faster ageing.
m: Passive cooling (natural airflow, floating PV) or active cooling
Use panels with a lower temperature coefficient, such as heterojunction cells
Add shading structures or reflective surfaces
Consider replacing panels with more efficient technologies

MEAS.imp: Crop losses, delayed planting, more disease, and disrupted collection and transport of feedstock.
m: Raise equipment and protect feedstock storage
Fit backflow preventers on biogas systems
Use nature-based solutions such as wetland restoration and flood-tolerant crops
Improve drainage and use farming practices that limit soil damage

MEAS.imp: Drier soils and poorer crop quality reduce yields. The same measures apply to heatwaves.
m: Promote drought-tolerant sugarcane varieties
Use efficient irrigation, such as drip and precision water management
Harvest rainwater and recycle wastewater
Mulch with crop residues to keep moisture in the soil
Assess biogas from urban organic waste in Santa Ana, San Salvador and San Miguel

MEAS.imp: Flood water damages wellheads and control systems.
m: Raise control and electrical systems
Build embankments and drainage to divert flood water

MEAS.imp: Shortage of cooling water reduces cooling efficiency and forces plants to run below capacity.
m: Adopt dry or hybrid cooling
Recycle water, for example reusing wastewater during droughts

MEAS.imp: Lower efficiency forces plants to run below capacity. Heat expansion can damage above-ground pipelines.
m: Plan dispatch around cooling water availability during heatwaves
Upgrade turbines, condensers and cooling towers to perform at high temperatures
Monitor conditions in real time and inspect cooling systems regularly
Expand on-site water storage drawing on several sources

MEAS.imp: Equipment damage, short circuits, corrosion, and failure of protection and control systems.
m: Raise switchgear and control rooms
Install flood barriers
Waterproof components where possible

MEAS.imp: Transformers overheat and lose efficiency and lifespan, raising the risk of failure. Derating them limits grid capacity.
m: Add or upgrade transformer cooling and maintain it
Install temperature monitoring
Add remotely operated switching linked to SCADA for fast fault isolation

MEAS.imp: Erosion of support structures. Soil movement can displace underground cables and stress their insulation.
m: Build flood-control infrastructure such as retention ponds
Improve insulator design to keep water out

MEAS.imp: Higher losses, lower line capacity and sagging lines.
m: Use dynamic line rating (DLR)
Increase line tension, or reconductor with high-temperature low-sag (HTLS) conductors
Underground critical sections
Manage vegetation near lines
Add remotely operated switching linked to SCADA

MEAS.imp: Damage to towers and erosion of their foundations.
m: Reinforce or raise tower foundations
Use flood-resistant materials
Divert flood water with embankments and drainage
Relocate sections on riverbanks or unstable slopes
Adjust dispatch and load to avoid overloading

MEAS.imp: Dry soil shrinks and cracks, weakening foundations.
m: Inspect and reinforce foundations
Use protective coatings or heat-resistant materials
Control vegetation around towers
